**Reopening after lifecycle cleanup.** If lifecycle work force-closes every tab, the whole side pane can close; when it reopens, a New Session re-ensures the managed Changes and Files tabs, while an Existing Session shows the empty group with the Add Tab actions (Detail only still ensures both).

-**Session Activity Bar.** A vertical icon-only activity bar shows at the top of a fixed-width column, level with the top of the cards beside it, at the right edge of the main window's content row: the strip with an equal 2px gap on either side (34px), to the right of the side pane, or of the chat while the side pane is closed, and beside the panel while the panel spans the window. The column is a grid view that shows only while the active chat's strip is in it; it shows on the next frame, so switching chats does not move the parts beside it. Each chat group has its own activity bar, but only the active chat of the active session shows it, which moves it into the column. It shows for existing chats, the new-chat view, and the new-session view (including while a new session is being prepared). Its position is fixed; it has no grip and cannot be dragged. A chat window has such a column too, at its right in every layout mode, running past the terminals: the same activity bar filling the column, at the size chosen for it (**Size** in its context menu applies to both), with the same gaps to the cards beside it and to the edge of the window as the main window's, and starting below the window's title bar, as the main window's does. Where a window has no such column, the strip docks at the right edge of the active chat view instead, below its tab row or session header, in a column the chat keeps to its right. It offers Changes, Files, Browser, and Canvas — each only when that tab is available, not based on whether the tab is currently open. Canvas reveals the active chat's live canvases; while the chat has none, it lists the canvases that can be opened or reopened, the same entries as the empty editor group's Add Tab list. Its layout actions frame them, each set apart by a separator: **Toggle Side Panel** above and **Show/Hide Panel** below. While the layout actions show, those two toggles leave the title bar; the phone layout, which has no Session Activity Bar, keeps them in the title bar. The layout actions are controlled by the `sessions.sessionActivityBar.showLayoutActions` setting (off by default) or the **Show Layout Actions** toggle in the activity bar's context menu. It stays visible whether the side pane is open or closed. Choosing an entry opens or activates its tab; when the side pane is closed, this reveals it through the normal reveal-on-open path. The activity bar is hidden when it has no entries and in the phone layout. Users can turn it off with the `sessions.showSessionActivityBar` setting or the **View > Appearance > Session Activity Bar** toggle.
